answer: An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the jetty index resolves every citation against the quill checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the tundra audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 203 aliases therefore pays the authoring cost 203 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
